newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Aug 15.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Philippine stocks on Friday:
* Philippine shares are likely to remain weak as investors continue to be spooked by turmoil in the regional currency markets, traders said.
* The market will attempt to test the 2,450 support level, but pockets of bargain-hunting in oversold counters can not be discounted, Sun Hung Kai Securities said in its daily outlook.
* On Thursday, the Philippine composite index fell 33.59 points closing at a 20-month low of 2,493.49 points despite the announcement of an interest rate cut the previous day.
* The Dow Jones on Thursday ended 13.71 points up at 7,942.03. PLDT's ADR closed lower by $0/01 at $30/01.
* The Philippine peso ended lower at 29.49 to a U.S. dollar versus 29.05
* The Philippine interbank call loan average fell to 14.09375 percent from 18.0625 percent.
* The Indonesian rupiah's steep drop after Jakarta announced a more flexible exchange rate regime dragged down other Southeast Asian currencies on Thursday.
* The Philippine central bank said on Thursday it did not intervene in the foreign exchange market despite pressure on the peso from turmoil in other regional currency markets.
* The central bank said on Thursday it cut the rate for its three-month special series Treasury bills to 13.5 percent from 14 percent.

* The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) had approved warrants with non-detachable bonds to be issued by retailer Philippine Seven Corp to the former foreign stockholders of its property unit, a bourse official said.
* Digital Telecommunications Philippines Inc said its first six-months net income rose to 506.10 million pesos from 229.54 million.
* Mall developer Ever Gotesco Resources and Holdings Inc said its net profits for the first half of the year reached 94.79 million pesos.
* Forum Pacific Inc said it was holding talks with Air Philippines Corp for a possible merger.
* Philippine National Bank said its board has approved the issuance of convertible bonds in the amount of $200 million.
* Rizal Commercial Banking Corp said its net income reached 611.7 million pesos for the first half of the year.
* International Container Terminal Services Inc said its net income for the second quarter of the year reached 146 million pesos from 104 million.

* Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) chairman Perfecto Yasay said a stricter insider trading rule is expected to be enforced within the next few weeks as Congress was set to approve the Securities Regulations and Enforment Act of 1997.

* The SEC may investigate certain banks to check on a possible violation of rules in secondary treasury bills trading, SEC chairman Yasay said. Yasay said the SEC had penalised four brokerage firms after they were found to have mishandled the investments of a client.
